subject: Implementation checkpoints: batching, routing, and quant profile alignment
messages:
From: Anna Li <anna@atlasai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Cost/perf kickoff + sample traffic

Hi Irene —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked for a short mutual action plan so our infra team can budget for the Dedicated slots if the numbers look good. To get the cost/perf estimates we can share a small sample of real traffic and a couple of target SLOs:

- Avg qps: ~12 (spikes to ~60 during batch jobs)
- Typical prompt length: 60–180 tokens
- Target latency P95: <= 350ms for interactive endpoints

I attached a sanitized traffic sample (atlas_traffic_sample.csv). Can your team outline the tuning checkpoints you’ll run during onboarding (batching, caching, quantization profiles, routing) and any data we should prepare?

Goal: get a scoped runbook and a cost delta estimate by Nov 6, so procurement can finish the monthly review.

Thanks,
Anna
Product Ops — AtlasAI
[Attachment: atlas_traffic_sample.csv (csv, 2.3MB)]

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Anna Li <anna@atlasai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cost/perf kickoff + sample traffic

Hi Anna —

Thanks for the sample and the clear SLOs. Quick plan from our side:

1) Intake (today–Nov 3)
- We’ll validate the sample, check token distribution, and confirm spike patterns.
- Request: can you include a small set of representative prompts for the P95 path (if different from average)?

2) Cost/perf baseline (Nov 3–4)
- Run baseline on hosted model variants to establish current per-token cost and latency.

3) Tuning sprint (Nov 5–9) — checkpoints at Nov 6 and Nov 9
- Batching: evaluate adaptive batching window vs fixed micro-batching; measure P95 impact and cost/unit.
- Caching: try prefix/KV caching for repeated context (we’ll estimate hit rate from sample).
- Quant profiles: test 4-bit and 8-bit candidates and measure quality delta on your eval prompts.
- Routing: simulate policy that routes low-latency interactive traffic to a smaller sequence-optimized variant and background jobs to quantized variants.

4) Deliverables (Nov 10)
- Short runbook with recommended config, expected cost delta, and rollback plan.
- Config snippets (console + API) and a staging rollout checklist.

I’ve looped Monica (CS lead) and Rishi (inference eng) for technical details and to own the checkpoints. We can do an internal sync tomorrow to align tasks.

Best,
Irene
Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cost/perf kickoff + sample traffic

Hi all —

Irene, thanks for the plan. I’ll run the tuning sprint and own checkpoints. To make the Nov 6 checkpoint actionable we need:

- Your top 20 production prompts (redacted is fine) for quality regression checks.
- A copy of your SLAs for background batch work that can tolerate higher latency.
- Confirmation of any PII/retention rules (so we can decide caching TTLs).

Preliminary internal checklist for Nov 6:
- Batching experiments:
  * Run adaptive batching (target window 15–40ms) and fixed micro-batch (N=8) on 1k sample requests; record P50/P95 and tokens/sec.
- Caching:
  * Estimate prefix hit rates from logs; run KV cache on repeated session flows.
- Quantization:
  * Evaluate two profiles: conservative (8-bit with per-channel scaling) and aggressive (4-bit asymmetric). Run 200 eval prompts and collect BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity delta.
- Routing policy sim:
  * Create synthetic routing split — 70% interactive to standard variant, 30% background to quantized. Measure cost and tail latency.

I’ll attach the cost worksheet and quant profile notes after the first run. If AtlasAI can provide a short window for a staging rollout (1–2 hours), we can validate telemetry and fallback behavior.

Thanks,
Monica
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_cost_profile_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Anna Li <anna@atlasai.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cost/perf kickoff + sample traffic

Quick technical notes from infra side —

- Tokenization: your sample shows a bimodal token distribution (short prompts ~40–60, long prompts ~150–200). For latency SLOs we should:
  * Prioritize short prompts on the low-latency pool with a lower batching window.
- KV caching: if session affinity exists, expect 18–27% hit rate — we’ll calculate exact from the 20 prompts once you share.
- Quantization risks: 4-bit aggressive profile introduces occasional lexical noise on long-form generation; we’ll gate that behind prompt-based quality checks.
- Autoscale safety: recommend a burst buffer of 30% for scheduled batch jobs to avoid congestion during daily spikes.

I’ve drafted quant_profiles.md with recommended flags for inference runtime (attached). I’ll also upload a small script to re-run your sample locally and produce per-route cost estimates.

—Rishi
Inference Engineering — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: quant_profiles.md (text, 18KB)]
